title: Pseudo-coherent complexes of locally finite Tor dimension are perfect
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and E an object of D(\mathcal O_X) [def-pc-derived-category]. If E is pseudo-coherent [def-pur-pseudo-coherent-complex] and locally has finite Tor dimension [def-pc-locally-finite-tor-dimension], then E is perfect [def-pc-perfect-complex].

proof.text: At each point intersect a pseudo-coherent finite-free model neighbourhood with a Tor neighbourhood. Refine their intersection to an affine open. Exact restriction preserves the model, its upper bound and free terms. Reuse the existing private affine_finiteFree_model theorem from PerfectOfPseudoCoherentFiniteTorDimension via import all to lift this model to a bounded-above finite-free ring complex.

The ring complex is pseudo-coherent by its own bounded-above finite-free representative. Transfer the local Tor bound using lem-pc-affine-local-sheafification-tor-amplitude, and apply lem-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-finite-tor-perfect.

Reuse the existing private affine_projective_strictlyPerfect theorem from PerfectOfPseudoCoherentFiniteTorDimension via import all: finite projectives split off finite free modules, and sheafification preserves the splitting and bounded zero terms. The affine localized derived comparison transports the derived isomorphism back to the original local model, witnessing perfectness at each point.
